title: New Tax Regime: 5 Ways to Reduce Your Tax for AY 2026-27
description: The new tax regime offers lower tax rates but limits traditional deductions, leading to a common misconception that no tax saving is possible. Salaried indivi.

faq.q: Can I claim Section 80C deductions under the new tax regime?
faq.a: No, most common deductions under Section 80C, such as investments in EPF, PPF, ELSS, life insurance premiums, and home loan principal repayment, are not available under the new tax regime.

faq.q: Is House Rent Allowance (HRA) exempt under the new tax regime?
faq.a: No, the exemption for House Rent Allowance (HRA) is not available under the new tax regime.

faq.q: Can I switch between the old and new tax regimes every year?
faq.a: Yes, salaried individuals can choose to switch between the old and new tax regimes each financial year. However, self-employed individuals or those with business income generally have a one-time option to switch out of the new regime, with specific conditions for re-opting.

faq.q: Is the Standard Deduction for salaried employees new for the new tax regime?
faq.a: Yes, for the new tax regime, the Standard Deduction of ₹50,000 for salaried individuals and pensioners was reintroduced from AY 2024-25 (FY 2023-24) onwards. It was not available in the initial version of the new regime.

faq.q: What if I have a home loan for a self-occupied property? Can I claim interest deduction?
faq.a: No, under the new tax regime, interest paid on a home loan for a self-occupied property is not deductible. This deduction is only available for interest paid on a home loan for a let-out (rented out) property.

faq.q: What is the maximum deduction allowed for employer's NPS contribution under Section 80CCD(2)?
faq.a: The maximum deduction allowed for an employer's contribution to NPS under Section 80CCD(2) is 10% of your basic salary plus Dearness Allowance (DA). For Central Government employees, this limit is 14%.
